runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for David O'Meara whose recent form of 9th, 13th, 11th, 12th in comparable Good-ground 7f races is deeply concerning; at seven years old and 38 days off the track, needs a truly strong pace to hunt down rivals on a front-runner-friendly surface, and that pace is unlikely to materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, Audience brings a strong speed figure and has run over today's trip and going before. He sits second on our figures here, though he is yet to score in his last six starts and a 38-day absence leaves a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has rediscovered his best form at 6-7f on Good ground, winning his last run and placing twice recently; W J Lee will look to sit handy in second or third off Power Blue's lead, and his sharp recent condition makes him one of the most dangerous tracking types in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, and a winner four starts back, Big Gossey heads our figures with a strong speed reading and has run over today's trip and going before. A below-form ninth three starts back is the blot, but he returns fresh 21 days on.

runners_data.name: East Hampton
runners_data.note: David Marnane's four-year-old has consecutive runner-up finishes at 7f in similar conditions and is a genuine prominent type who should sit just off the pace; the step back to Good to Firm from softer ground on his last two runs is a positive, and Luke McAteer is well placed to keep him in a clean position.
runners_data.comment: A second two starts back, and a second five starts back, underline East Hampton's consistency, and he has run over today's trip before. That profile makes him our pick, though he is yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Zodiac Bear
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old has two wins and two places from five outings at this trip and going combination, giving him strong profile credentials — however, the crowded prominent division means Ben Coen will likely find him further back than ideal, and his chance is contingent on threading through without losing momentum.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, and a winner four starts back, Zodiac Bear has recent form on his side and has run over today's trip before. But he sits second-bottom of our figures with a modest speed reading, making him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: A persistent winning type at 7-8f on Good ground for Daniel McLoughlin, with four wins from his last five at those trips, but he races here only 10 days after his last run and — crucially — will be pushed wider in the pack than his front-running tendencies demand, making his true form hard to express from a compromised early position.
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, and a winner three starts back, Duckadilly returns quickly here on just 10 days and has run over today's trip and going before. But she sits bottom of our figures, with modest efforts either side of those wins.

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's lightly-raced three-year-old carries a five-pound age allowance and won back-to-back on Soft ground earlier in his career, but his last three runs on Good have produced 9th, 8th, and 7th; Ryan Moore will likely try to get him closer than the pace map allows, but his recent Good-ground form suggests the surface itself may be an issue beyond just positioning.
runners_data.comment: Dorset was a winner four starts back, and a winner five starts back, but a below-form ninth last time out means recent starts have trended the wrong way. He has run over today's trip and going before and holds a fair speed figure, rated mid-pack here.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Robson De Aguiar, trained to lead and run his own race — Rossa Ryan will take Power Blue straight to the front, and with no credible challenger for the lead, sets the tempo entirely on his own terms; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects he holds his position by default rather than dominance, but an uncontested lead on fast ground over 7f is a powerful tactical asset regardless.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, and a second four starts back, Power Blue matches that placed form with a big speed figure and has run over today's trip and going before. Back-to-back fourths in his last two starts are the one blot.

races.paceDynamic: Power Blue is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh over 7f, is likely to stride straight to the lead and set a controlled, honest but not frenetic gallop — crucially, without a genuine rival to push him along. Big Gossey and East Hampton are the legitimate prominent types who will sit closest to Power Blue, tracking in second and third, while Zodiac Bear, Duckadilly, and Dorset — all natural prominent racers — are squeezed into a midfield cluster they would not naturally occupy because the race simply cannot accommodate five horses in the front three. Audience, a hold-up type, will be last or near-last from the outset and faces the biggest ask on a track that, while fair, rewards those with early position on a fast surface. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours the horse who can dictate or sit closest to a single, uncontested leader, making Power Blue and the tracking pair of Big Gossey and East Hampton the best-placed profiles — true hold-up running is structurally disadvantaged here, and the redistributed prominent types may find themselves in traffic at a critical point.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Power Blue Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Power Blue is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop and quickens on his own terms from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Power Blue sets fractions he is comfortable with on Good to Firm and never faces a serious challenge for the lead, meaning his stamina reserves are intact when he kicks; the trackers Big Gossey and East Hampton are best placed to benefit if he weakens late, but if his class holds, the leader is very hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Big Gossey or East Hampton press Power Blue enough to empty him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger pace sees Power Blue tied up close home, handing the initiative to the most alert of the tracking pair; Big Gossey's recent winning form over 6f-7f on Good ground and East Hampton's runner-up profile in similar conditions give both the profile to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded midfield bunch — Zodiac Bear, Duckadilly, Dorset — creates interference or forces a wide passage that burns pace from an unexpected source.
scenarios.body: One of the displaced prominent types forces through on the outside earlier than ideal, injecting a mid-race surge that scrambles the race shape and opens a gap for a horse with residual energy; Zodiac Bear, who has the best form figures at this trip and going combination of the three, is most likely to capitalise if he can find daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses sharply in the final 2f and Audience is able to weave through a wall of tiring bodies.
scenarios.body: Audience would need a combination of fast early fractions exhausting the field and a clear run materialising almost simultaneously — both are unlikely given the controlled single-leader tempo anticipated; a seven-year-old with a recent form string showing double-figure finishes in similar conditions makes this the lowest-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Power Blue's early stride pattern — if Rossa Ryan is forced wider than stall position suggests or Big Gossey comes out fast beside him, even a brief early duel could fundamentally change this race shape and undermine the dominant scenario.

Zodiac Bear and Duckadilly both attempting to push forward from redistributed midfield positions in the first furlong could create a bunching incident on the stands side, putting East Hampton in particular at risk of a checked run.

Dorset's going form — three consecutive finishes of 7th-or-worse on Good ground raise a genuine question about whether Ryan Moore will be able to produce a forward move even if he gets a clean run, potentially turning a tactical note into a form issue.

Audience's sectional position in the final 2f is worth monitoring purely as a pace barometer — if she makes any meaningful ground on the leaders, it signals the early pace was stronger than anticipated and that the redistribution chaos scenario (C) carries more live weight than its 9% probability suggests.

Big Gossey's age (nine) means his condition sharpness from a 21-day break is a key watch — if he travels smoothly in the first half of the race and his ears are pricked, the tracking scenario is firmly on; if he is ridden along before the turn, discount him quickly.

races.name: Racing World 50th Anniversary Irish EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Orchidaceae
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with a sharp form profile — her one win in this race came over 7f on Good but she has solid placed form at the mile, and sim-going figures of 8/9 on comparable ground represent the strongest going record in the field; headgear (p) unchanged, 22 days since last run is fresh enough.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's trip and going before, with a winner four starts back the stand-out form line. Fit for a break of 22 days, she's clearly the one to beat from stall 6 on our figures despite a below-par run last time out.

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare who has failed to win in recent form (-00356) and carries blinkers, but her three placed efforts over this trip and going suggest she stays competitive; a 37-day absence and a trainer sending out just 1 from 5 in the last fortnight are mild flags.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's distance before and was placed third three starts back, a solid form line for this grade. Winless in her last five starts and up against it after a 37-day break, but she remains a leading danger from stall 1 on figures.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here, Colin Keane takes the ride for the high-strike G M Lyons yard (5/26 last 14 days) — her record over 8f on Good-type ground is acceptable (2W4P in 15 starts), though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects she is racing at her shorter limits for this field, and pace pressure from closer types should be monitored.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, and a third four starts back, useful form for this grade. Has run over today's trip and going before, and remains winless in her last five starts, but that placed effort makes her one to note from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Sanctijude
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a pivotal win over 8f on Good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle booked — her form string (-43417) shows a recent dip but the mile and conditions are right; 21 days since last run and tongue-tie headgear both noted for an unexposed filly who could be well-handicapped off OR 81.
runners_data.comment: Sanctijude was a winner two starts back, and a third four starts back, form that puts her firmly in this contest. She has run over today's distance before, though a seventh last time out is the main concern from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip at the Curragh on Good ground on her last winning start, giving her a strong course-and-distance profile — her natural game is to race prominently, but with Mallavelly already filling that role the JP O'Brien-trained filly is likely to be pushed slightly back from where she travels best, which tempers confidence despite the appealing recent form (07571 ending in a win).
runners_data.comment: Ranks bottom of our figures here, with modest form beyond a win last time out. The yard is in good form at 36% over the last fortnight, and she has run over today's distance before, but there's plenty to prove from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer on Good and Standard ground who brings live form figures (3-2-5-1-2) and experience over this course and distance — her instinct is to race up with the pace, but the field's structure means she is unlikely to secure her favoured berth; Mrs John Harrington's yard is cold (0/24 last 14 days), and a 6-day turnaround adds a minor fitness query for a filly already asked to race out of her comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Often placed in recent starts, with a win four starts back, though the yard is out of form, blank in its last 24 runners. Quick back after 6 days and has run over today's distance before, but stable form is a concern from stall 2.

races.paceDynamic: Mallavelly is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a six-runner field, she is set to control this race from the front at a sustainable, unflustered tempo on Good to Firm ground. Sanctijude and Kirkland Sioux carry prominent profiles but, with Mallavelly already occupying that role and the field compressed, they are unlikely to race in their natural position — Mallavelly is most likely to secure the lead uncontested, with Sanctijude potentially slotting in second and Kirkland Sioux and Glitter And Glory, both natural prominent types, pushed back against their instincts into midfield. The hold-up pair Orchidaceae and Pink Oxalis will track from the rear, relying on a strong final-furlong kick on a flat, undemanding track that historically rewards those who can quicken off a steady gallop. This race shape — a controlled, single-pace-setter scenario on fast ground — most favours horses with a proven turn of foot who can pick up off a genuine but uncontested tempo, tilting the tactical balance toward prominent racers who get close to Mallavelly early and stay competitive into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mallavelly Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mallavelly leads unchallenged throughout and the pace stays honest but not excessive, denying closers a clean run at her.
scenarios.body: Mallavelly dictates on the front end with Colin Keane setting a metronomic tempo, and any horse that tracks her closely through the race is best placed to pounce; a flat mile at Curragh in fast ground rewards those who conserve energy near the pace rather than making up ground from far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker such as Sanctijude or Kirkland Sioux sits a length or two off Mallavelly and produces a clean, well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sanctijude, with winning form over a mile in Good conditions and a strong jockey booking in Dylan Browne McMonagle, is ideally suited to latching onto the leader's heels and overhauling her late; Kirkland Sioux's recent Curragh win over this trip on Good ground also makes her dangerous in this shape if she can recover her natural position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Swoop From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If Mallavelly's pace proves genuinely quick enough to stretch the field and create a gap for the hold-up horses to exploit late.
scenarios.body: Orchidaceae has the best recent form profile in similar going conditions with three wins and three places in nine comparable-going runs, and a strong finishing kick would make her dangerous in this shape; Pink Oxalis has the class to be competitive but her record in similar going is modest and she faces a significant ground to make up from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Glitter And Glory Finds Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If Glitter And Glory overcomes her natural prominent style being compressed into midfield and produces an uncharacteristically strong sustained run through the straight.
scenarios.body: Glitter And Glory has consistent placed form on Good ground and over this trip, but her style-fit concern and a cold trainer strike rate of 0/24 in the last 14 days are material headwinds; this scenario depends on her racing well out of role, which the evidence tags as unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Mallavelly — if Colin Keane finds the front unchallenged as expected, watch whether she is allowed to roll along at her own pace or is pressured early by Sanctijude, as that distinction will determine whether she holds on or fades inside the final furlong.

Sanctijude — Dylan Browne McMonagle is likely to try to position her directly behind Mallavelly; if she gets a clean passage into the straight on the flat Curragh mile, she is the most dangerous individual to the leader given her win over this trip and going.

Kirkland Sioux and Glitter And Glory — both are genuine prominent types who will not find their natural position in this race; watch whether either attempts to push forward early and thereby inject more pace than the current map assumes, which would reorder the pace scenario entirely.

Orchidaceae — with the best sim-going record in the field (8/9), she is the hold-up runner most likely to benefit if the pace collapses late, but she must generate momentum from the back of a small field with few horses to track — her run-style in this shape is inherently high-risk.

Pink Oxalis — 37 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; if she shows any fitness concern in the preliminary stages or fails to travel smoothly for Jack Kearney (3), her chances of landing a late blow from the rear diminish sharply.

races.name: 1xBet.ie Proud Supporters Of Irish Racing Curragh Cup (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Al Riffa
runners_data.note: Six-year-old confirmed front-runner for Joseph O'Brien, taking on a step up from 1m4f; Dylan Browne McMonagle rides and if he dictates a modest gallop the horse is dangerous, though a STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 reflects he is best when setting his own terms rather than racing in company.|
runners_data.comment: Al Riffa leads the way on our figures and owns the best speed figure in this race, and has run over today's trip and going before. Yet to win in his last five starts, a third two starts back marks him out as capable, and that edge makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type who finds himself better placed in this race shape than most; best effort came at 2m on Good, suggesting stamina is his weapon, and Rossa Ryan will be patient before asking for an effort.|
runners_data.comment: A close second four starts back is the highlight of Dallas Star's recent efforts, though a below-form seventh last time out is a concern. He has run over today's trip and going before, and yet to win in his last six starts, he rates fairly enough for minor honours.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's four-year-old has solid Good-ground form but has spent recent starts at 10f-12f — the step to 1m6f is an important unknown; naturally prominent but the crowded front-running picture means Shane Foley may have to accept a more restrained role than the horse prefers, which tempers confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Green Impact was a winner five starts back and carries a strong speed figure into this, sitting fourth on our ratings. Three fourths have followed that, and a 56-day absence is the obvious question mark now.

runners_data.name: Happy Pharoah
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's four-year-old has placed twice at 1m4f in good company and won at 1m3f, so the 1m6f trip is unproven territory; he races with a tongue-tie and, being a true prominent type squeezed out of his favoured berth by this pace-rich field, Paddy Harnett may find himself further back than ideal with 65 days between runs.|
runners_data.comment: Happy Pharoah was runner-up last time out, and a winner four starts back, form that hints at ability, but he is second-bottom of our figures here with a modest speed reading. He has run over today's distance before, though a 65-day absence since his last run is another concern.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this five-year-old for A P O'Brien, and he arrives in good order having won over 2m2f Good last time out; his form profile suggests genuine stamina, he handles the good-ground surface well, and he is one of the few horses whose natural prominent style maps cleanly onto the expected race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, Illinois backs that up with the second-best figure and a strong speed reading, and he has run over today's trip and going before. A seventh four starts back is the one blemish in an otherwise progressive picture.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Stud
runners_data.note: J M Sheridan's four-year-old won at 1m7f on Heav before a poor effort on Good most recently; he is a naturally front-running type who loses his position here due to traffic at the head of affairs, and the 51 days since his last run adds a question mark over sharpness.|
runners_data.comment: A third last time out follows a winning effort three starts back for Tennessee Stud, form that puts him mid-table on our figures with a fair speed reading. A blank two starts back and a 51-day absence since are the concerns holding him back here.

runners_data.name: Trustyourinstinct
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has been in fine form for Joseph O'Brien, with two seconds and a win from his last four; Declan McDonogh has ridden him regularly, he acts well on Good ground at around 1m2f, and the step up to 1m6f is the one note of caution for an otherwise well-placed runner.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, Trustyourinstinct carries solid recent form and the third-best rating in this field into the race. A pair of below-form efforts four and five starts back stand out as the blot, but he returns quickly on just 21 days.

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this JP Murtagh four-year-old who is lightly weighted at 134lbs and was a good winner over 1m4f Good 11 days ago; her natural prominence is her strength but she enters a field with too many front-runners to get her preferred slot easily, though she brings strong recent form and the quick turnaround after a confident victory is a positive sign.|
runners_data.comment: Winner last time out, and a winner four starts back, Floresta returns quickly here on just 11 days and has run over today's distance before. But she sits bottom of our figures with a modest speed reading to match, leaving her hard to fancy despite that form.

races.paceDynamic: Al Riffa is the confirmed front-runner here, and with only one genuine pace-setter in an eight-runner field over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh, he is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, measured tempo without significant pressure. Illinois and Trustyourinstinct will look to sit prominently just behind, with the remaining pack — including those redistributed further back — tracking through the middle. The race is likely to develop into a steadily-run affair until Al Riffa quickens entering the straight, where those with the tactical speed to respond from just off the pace will hold a distinct advantage over true hold-up operators. This race shape strongly favours those racing close to, but not at, the pace — horses able to track Al Riffa's controlled gallop and sustain a challenge over the final two furlongs, making Illinois and Trustyourinstinct the best-positioned profiles. Several runners — Tennessee Stud, Green Impact, Floresta, and Happy Pharoah — are naturally prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred position, and one or two will be forced to race in a more restrained role than suits them, compressing the midfield and muddying the hold-up picture.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clear Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Al Riffa dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and has enough in reserve to quicken decisively once the field turns for home.
scenarios.body: Al Riffa controls the tempo entirely, denying rivals a true test of stamina, and his prominent-tracking pursuers Illinois and Trustyourinstinct are best placed to challenge as he turns for home; the Good to Firm ground suits a race run at an honest but not brutal gallop, rewarding tactical speed over pure stayability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Al Riffa sets an overly slow pace that compresses the field and allows genuine hold-up runners to produce a late burst.
scenarios.body: A crawl up front bunches the field and turns the race into a sprint over the final furlong, nullifying the prominently-drawn advantage and opening the door for Dallas Star or any runner who can find an unobstructed run late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Gallop Suits Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If redistributed prominent types press Al Riffa from early, lifting the tempo and transforming this into a true stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop filters out the less genuine stayers and rewards runners with the deepest reserves over 1m6f on fast ground; Illinois's recent winning form over this distance and Floresta's progressive profile at the trip make them the prime beneficiaries of a searching pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Out-of-Role Runners Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent types push to the front early and create an unexpectedly erratic or high-tempo race.
scenarios.body: Tennessee Stud, Green Impact or Happy Pharoah force a chaotic early pace that upsets the expected race shape, leaving those who settle smoothly in midfield as the race falls apart in the straight; in this fractured scenario class and finishing power over the trip become the deciding factors.

watchPoints.text: Al Riffa's pace — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle sends him clear immediately or allows the field to compress, as that single decision will determine whether this is a true test of stamina or a sprint for home.|

Tennessee Stud, Green Impact, and Happy Pharoah are all naturally prominent types who cannot all find their position; jostling in the early stages for the rail or a prominent berth could create a fractured early gallop and cause trouble in the first half-mile.|
Trustyourinstinct is unproven beyond 1m2f — watch how he travels as the pace settles over the back straight, as any sign of labouring before the turn will indicate the trip stretching his stamina.|

Dallas Star is the only true hold-up runner in the field; if the pace is anything other than very slow he should get his ground-gaining opportunity late, but Rossa Ryan will need a clean run from the outside gate.|

Floresta's quick turnaround (11 days) is worth monitoring in the paddock — she won well last time, but back-to-back efforts within a fortnight at Group 2 level against older horses over a longer trip merits observation before the race.|

races.name: James Nolan Bar Kildare Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is a useful weight advantage, and two of his last four runs have come on Good ground with a course win in his profile — the key question is whether 52 days off has left him short, but Michael Mulvany sends him here as the clear pace-controlling force.
runners_data.comment: Lars Soldier was a winner three starts back and third last time out, form that stands out in this field. He has run over today's distance before, and despite 52 days off, he looks clear of these on figures from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's yard is in solid form with four winners from 14 runners over the past fortnight, and this filly has placed three times in four starts including over 6f on Good ground — she wears headgear and is drawn to press the leader, which is her most natural position.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, third last time out and second two starts back, a leading threat here. He has run over today's distance before and is fit having run 16 days ago, though he remains winless in his last four starts from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Desert Alchemist
runners_data.note: David Marnane's hold-up type has her best form at 6f including a third on soft, and while she has only finished in the frame once from three starts, she is lightly raced and the step up to 6f on faster ground could play to a mid-race effort; naturally off the pace, she needs plenty to go right.
runners_data.comment: Desert Alchemist was placed third three starts back but has since finished sixth and eighth, a mixed picture heading into this. He has run over today's distance before and returns 23 days after that run, leaving him a fair midfield contender from stall 3.

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant jockey booking for a horse who has finished no better than fifth in three starts all on Good ground at 6f, and the form figures — 8-5-6 — offer very little encouragement; a true hold-up runner who has yet to find any late momentum in this type of race.
runners_data.comment: I Ready is rated above his official mark on our figures and is quick to return, just 8 days after his latest outing. He has run over today's distance before, but his recent form reads eighth, fifth and sixth, leaving him winless in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner carries a ⚠ fade flag and has finished sixth, eighth, and eighth in his last three outings including two on Good — naturally a hold-up type, he is mapped to midfield here only because the field is congested at the rear, and 61 days off adds a further concern for a horse whose finishing effort has consistently disappointed.
runners_data.comment: Seven Nation Army's recent form of sixth and two eighths is modest, and a 61-day absence adds to the concern. The yard is in good form though, striking at 36% over the last fortnight, and he has run over today's distance before from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar has drawn a blank with 12 runners over the past fortnight, and Belle Island has only one run on Good ground from four starts (finishing tenth) — her better form came on Standard and yielding surfaces, making the fast going a legitimate concern for a horse who is a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield by field congestion.
runners_data.comment: Belle Island was placed third three starts back and second four starts back, solid form for this level. She has run over today's distance before and is fit from a recent run, though an unplaced effort last time out is the main concern from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Lucy's Promise
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's booking adds some interest, but Lucy's Promise has finished sixth, seventh, and twelfth in three starts all on Good ground at 6f and 8f — a natural off-the-pace runner shifted forward on this map by default, she has shown no signs of the late kick needed to trouble the front rank in this or any similar race.
runners_data.comment: Lucy's Promise is our lowest-rated runner here, with no placed effort in her last three starts. She has run over today's distance before and returns quickly after just 8 days, but the overall form gives little to work with from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.note: Trained by J P Murtagh, who has two winners from 22 runners in the past 14 days, Woodlawn Lily has form figures of 4-6-7 and steps up to 6f for the first time from 5f — a genuine hold-up horse who is shown in midfield only because the rear is overcrowded, and the trip extension is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Woodlawn Lily's form has trended the wrong way, with finishes of seventh, sixth and fourth in her last three starts. She has run over today's distance before and is fit from a recent run, but there's no placed effort to work with from stall 2.

races.paceDynamic: Lars Soldier is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to force the pace, will slide into an uncontested lead from the front, dictating a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over six furlongs. Tradewinds will press from a prominent position to his outside, but without a challenger matching Lars Soldier stride for stride early, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. Behind them, Seven Nation Army, Belle Island, Lucy's Promise, and Woodlawn Lily are all genuine hold-up types pushed forward on the map because the field carries more off-the-pace runners than can realistically race from the rear — in practice, most will settle in a tightly-bunched midfield group with little genuine cover. This race shape strongly favours Lars Soldier and Tradewinds, who will dictate terms from the front and be hardest to peg back on a flat, fast track where a controlled lead is rarely surrendered cheaply at six furlongs at the Curragh.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lars Soldier leads from flag fall and is allowed to dictate a regulated pace with no serious early pressure.
scenarios.body: Lars Soldier sets his own fractions on Good to Firm ground, rationing his effort through the first four furlongs before quickening under Wesley Joyce to maintain a decisive advantage; the field, bunched and without a genuine presser, is left chasing shadows. Prominent types nearest to the pace are best placed to chase, but the leader's controlled energy expenditure through the early stages is the decisive tactical edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Out
scenarios.trigger: If Tradewinds presses Lars Soldier hard enough to force a genuine pace duel that sets up a straight fight between the two.
scenarios.body: The two horses at the head of affairs run a proper race at each other through the middle portion, leaving both slightly vulnerable late — but the strongest of the pair wins a contested finish as the hold-up horses fail to close from too far back on fast ground. Tradewinds, with recent 6f form and a yard in strong shape over the fortnight, is positioned to benefit most if Lars Soldier fades.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swallows Leaders Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the leaders tie up inside the final furlong, gifting a late-finishing type a rare winning opportunity.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse would need to find the field strung out and the front-runners emptying — an unlikely scenario given the lack of natural pace pressure in this race, but Desert Alchemist and Seven Nation Army have both shown the ability to pick up from mid-division on similar ground. The scenario is discounted because the redistributed runners are not true closers in nature and the pace is expected to be steady rather than burning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Compresses Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a muddled, slowly-run affair that sees the whole field race in a cluster and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: In a race run at modest tempo, raw speed off the bend decides matters and the horse with the clearest passage and most residual energy wins in a bunch finish. Belle Island and Woodlawn Lily hold each-way claims only in this scenario, but their recent form figures make them very marginal beneficiaries at best.

watchPoints.text: Lars Soldier's price and fate hinge on whether Wesley Joyce can find an uncontested lead within the first furlong — watch the draw and early stride, because any crowding away from the gates could cost him the initiative that makes him dangerous.

Tradewinds is wearing headgear and represents a yard in form; if she tracks Lars Soldier closely rather than pressing, she becomes the most likely beneficiary if the leader flattens out in the final 100 yards.

Seven Nation Army carries a pace-fade flag and has disappointed badly in three straight starts — Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite jockey but the horse's own pattern of fading late on Good ground should temper any confidence in a revival here at 61 days off.

The Going Report confirms Good to Firm at 5:00 rather than the listed Good — this is meaningful for Desert Alchemist, whose sole form hint came on soft ground, and may reduce the likelihood of any late-finishing type sustaining a meaningful challenge in the straight.

Four runners in this field are genuine hold-up types all competing for the same ground at the back of the pack; watch for traffic and interference inside the final two furlongs if they all come wide simultaneously in search of a clear run.
